unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Rename `platform init/status --output` to `--root` (keep `--output` as a hidden deprecated alias for one release), and converge `--out`/`--out-dir` onto `--output` with deprecated aliases. A small table in docs/cli-reference.md stating the flag-naming conventions (--output writes, --catalog reads, --root anchors) would lock it in.

unverifiedFindings.title: Browse surface duplicated: `catalog inspect` is a hidden alias of `inspect`, `diff` and `catalog diff` reuse one verb for different semantics, and there is no `catalog list`
unverifiedFindings.detail: `newCatalogInspectCmd` simply calls `runInspect(args[0])` — byte-identical behavior to top-level `inspect`, but neither help text says they are the same command, and the pair share the package-global `inspectOpts`. Meanwhile top-level `diff` compares two versioned releases of one image while `catalog diff` compares two catalog directories — same verb, different semantics — and `list` has no `catalog list` counterpart, so the symmetry a user might infer does not hold.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Make aliasing explicit: either register the same *cobra.Command in both places with `Short: "Alias of clearcutt inspect"`, or drop `catalog inspect` with a deprecation notice. Rename `catalog diff` to something self-describing like `catalog diff-dirs` or clarify both Short strings ("compare two releases of one image" vs "compare two generated catalog directories").

unverifiedFindings.title: All failures exit 1: CI cannot distinguish a policy-gate failure from an operational error
unverifiedFindings.detail: main.go already special-cases the sentinel: `if !errors.Is(err, commands.ErrCheckFailed) { fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, ...) }; os.Exit(1)`. Fifteen gating commands return `ErrCheckFailed`, so the distinction between "the image failed policy" and "the catalog file was unreadable" exists in-process but is flattened to exit code 1 at the boundary. CI consumers (the project's core audience) cannot tell a gate verdict from a crashed tool without parsing stderr.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Map `ErrCheckFailed` to a documented distinct exit code (e.g., 1 = checks failed, 2 = usage/operational error, matching conftest/OPA conventions), document it in docs/cli-reference.md, and add a drift-script `help_contains` style assertion. The sentinel plumbing makes this a ~5 line change in main.go.

unverifiedFindings.title: Hardcoded `cliReleaseTag = 'v0.10.2'` in the site CLI page is a manual version pin outside the doc-drift gate
unverifiedFindings.detail: `const cliReleaseTag = 'v0.10.2';` is hand-maintained in both the live site page and the embedded sitetemplate copy. The doc-drift gate only bans one historical bad pin in markdown docs (`check_absent "v0.11.1" "documented ClearCutt release pins must point at a published release"`), so the Astro pages' pinned tag can silently fall behind actual releases — a known drift class in this repo (local tags reach v0.9.8 while the page pins v0.10.2).
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Derive the tag from catalog data like the page already does for `imageReleaseTag` (`index?.latestTag`), falling back to a single source-of-truth constant; or extend validate-doc-commands.sh to assert the two cli.astro pins match a version recorded in one place.

unverifiedFindings.title: No self-contained contributor environment: core devShell omits Go/Node, and the repo that ships devcontainers for app teams has none for itself
unverifiedFindings.detail: The default devShell's buildInputs are git, curl, patchelf, cosign, trivy, grype, syft, skopeo, container-structure-test — image-gating tools only. A contributor still needs Go 1.26 (bleeding-edge per cli/go.mod), Node for site/, and Python 3 for core tests, each installed out-of-band. Every app template ships a `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` pinned to a ClearCutt dev image, but the platform repo itself has no root devcontainer or all-in-one shell, so the "clone and be productive" promise depends on four separately installed toolchains.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Add `hostPkgs.go`, `hostPkgs.nodejs`, and `hostPkgs.python3` to the default devShell (or add a `devShells.contrib`), and/or commit a root `.devcontainer` so `nix develop ./core` or one container is the single onboarding step CONTRIBUTING.md can point at.

unverifiedFindings.title: `platform init --force` clobbers fork customizations with no preview
unverifiedFindings.detail: FORKING.md tells fork owners to run `./clearcutt platform init --owner YOUR_ORG --repo YOUR_REPO --force` on first setup. `writeGeneratedFile` with force=true unconditionally overwrites `clearcutt.yaml`, `docs/platform-kit.md`, `core/lib/platform-metadata.nix`, and all four app template trees. A fork operator who re-runs init later (e.g., after a registry rename) silently destroys any local edits to those generated files; `localizeConsumerExamples` is careful to edit examples in place, but the generated files get full rewrites. There is no --dry-run or diff mode.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Add `--dry-run` that prints the would-write/would-localize file list (the function already accumulates `written`/`localized` slices, so this is mostly a write-suppression flag), and have non-dry runs print a one-line warning when overwriting a file that differs from the generated content.

strengths: Real, independently verifiable evidence is committed and live, not fixture theater: site/src/data/catalog/ holds the generated v0.10.2 catalog with Rekor transparency log indexes (e.g. transparencyLogIndex 1749384161 with a search.sigstore.dev link in site/src/data/catalog/images/java21-distroless.json), GitHub Actions run URLs, per-arch SBOMs (syft-1.44.0, 120 packages with purl+CPE), grype findings with dbBuiltAt and KEV status, and GitHub Release asset URLs for raw SBOM/provenance/test JSON. The portal serves machine-readable evidence at /catalog/evidence-manifest.json and /catalog/images/<id>.json (verified live, HTTP 200). A skeptical reviewer can run the cosign/gh-attestation commands the docs print and cross-check the catalog record — exactly the differentiation claim made in docs/alternatives.md ('inspectable evidence surfaces rather than opaque trust').

Docs are CI-tested, not aspirational: scripts/validate-doc-commands.sh (invoked at .github/workflows/pr-gate.yml:376) executes command snippets from README.md and 10 docs against the built CLI. My own spot-check of 10 cross-references (verify rebuild flags in cli/internal/commands/verify_rebuild.go:144-156, platform status --output/--fleet-config in platform.go:54-69, catalog build --scan-depth in catalog_build.go:40, dev --devcontainer/--print in dev.go:77-82, exceptions --fail-on-expired-exceptions, vex --tag, graftOntoBase in core/flake.nix:197, agent-sandbox.sh, OPENROUTER_API_KEY in cve-patch-agent.yml:93, CLEARCUTT_G2_* in core/tests/verify.sh) found zero drift, and a link-check of all relative doc links found zero dead links. The README 'First Proof' commands actually run green from a clean clone.

Claim discipline is unusually rigorous for an OSS security project: docs/audit-findings.md is a formal claims register ('safe core claims' vs 'claims requiring caveats'), docs/homepage-audit.md audits homepage copy against reality, site/src/pages/limitations.astro documents eight concrete boundaries (RPATH leakage, fail-closed admission risk, OpenShift runAsGroup:0, credential exposure on build nodes), and the verify-image-vs-verify-release-evidence distinction (catalog gate vs registry-side crypto) is held consistently across README.md:61-64, docs/concepts/mental-model.md:54-60, and docs/trust/evidence-walkthrough.md.

docs/trust/cve-agent-threat-model.md is a genuinely good agent threat model: it treats advisory prose as prompt-injection-capable input, names the sandbox (core/scripts/agent-sandbox.sh — exists), requires validate-overlays + build/scan proof + human merge authority, and lists explicit non-claims. AI patch drafting is correctly opt-in (workflow_dispatch + OPENROUTER_API_KEY secret in .github/workflows/cve-patch-agent.yml).

Deep engineering hygiene that deserves marketing: the Astro portal is embedded into the Go binary via go:generate with a drift test (cli/internal/sitetemplate/sitetemplate.go — 'TestEmbeddedTemplateMatchesSite drift test fails if it falls out of sync'), so one binary scaffolds a complete evidence portal; the closure-equivalence in-toto predicate (https://clearcutt.dev/attestations/closure-equivalence/v1, docs/enterprise-compliance.md:77-82) is a novel, falsifiable attestation for BYO-base grafts; and the rebase flow's dual-identity trust boundary (developer signature verified before rebase-engine re-signs, docs/security-model.md:60-79) is articulated more honestly than most commercial offerings.
wowIdeas: A CI-generated 'receipts' page that makes alternatives.md undeniable: nightly workflow builds/pulls the same hello-service image on clearcutt-java21:distroless, eclipse-temurin:21-jre, gcr.io/distroless/java21-debian12, and a Chainguard JRE, then publishes compressed size, package count, SBOM package depth (syft), critical/high CVE counts with scan date (grype), and which cosign/slsa-verifier commands succeed for each — rendered as a portal page and a committed markdown table. Every tool needed (syft, grype, crane, catalog renderer) is already in the pipeline.

A 'Verify this page yourself' block on every image detail page: the catalog records already contain the Rekor transparencyLogIndex, workflow identity, and digest — emit a single copy-paste script per image that runs cosign verify + gh attestation verify + jq-compares the registry result against the rendered catalog record, turning the portal into a self-auditing artifact. Link the Rekor entry (transparencyUrl is already in the data) as a clickable 'public transparency log' badge.

Promote the self-audit machinery as a product feature: docs/audit-findings.md (claims register), docs/homepage-audit.md, and the pr-gate doc-snippet validation (scripts/validate-doc-commands.sh) are a unique 'docs-as-tests + claims-as-policy' story no competitor tells. A short 'How ClearCutt audits its own claims' page on the portal — with the pr-gate badge wired to the actual drift checks — converts the currently-risky docs/analysis history into the project's most distinctive trust signal.

Ship the fixture-backed demo as a recorded artifact and a one-command experience: `make demo` (or `clearcutt demo`) that runs the five clean-clone proof commands and opens the locally built portal against internal/testdata/mixed-catalog, paired with an asciinema-GIF in the README hero. The deterministic fixtures make the recording reproducible, and it collapses the time-to-wow for an HN visitor from ten minutes of reading to thirty seconds of watching.

verifiedFindings.title: docs/alternatives.md never makes the technical case — the differentiation doc is the weakest page in the repo
verifiedFindings.detail: The designated manager entry point ('First document' for Engineering manager in README.md:73) is 43 lines and never names a single alternative: no apko/Chainguard, no gcr.io/distroless, no plain pkgs.dockerTools, no Docker multi-stage. The comparison table is four generic categories ('Vendor hardened feed | Operationally simple... | Less ownership...') with zero numbers — no closure size, package count, CVE delta, SBOM depth, or provenance-verifiability comparison, even though the repo already generates all of those metrics per image (latestPackageCount, vulnSummary, sbom.packages in site/src/data/catalog). The repo's own audit (docs/analysis/decisions-needed.md) chose 'category-level tradeoff comparison' deliberately, but for a wow-factor showcase the result reads as hand-wavy: a reader cannot tell why ClearCutt distroless beats a hand-rolled dockerTools.buildLayeredImage or a Chainguard image on any measurable axis. The capping irony: the manager's 'first useful command' is `sed -n '1,140p' docs/alternatives.md` — printing 140 lines of a 43-line file.
verifiedFindings.recommendation: Add a CI-generated comparison artifact and link it from alternatives.md: a scheduled job that builds/pulls the same Java 21 service on (a) clearcutt-java21:distroless, (b) eclipse-temurin:21-jre, (c) gcr.io/distroless/java21-debian12, (d) a Chainguard JRE image, then publishes a table of compressed size, package count, syft SBOM package depth, grype critical/high counts with scan date, and which signature/provenance verification commands succeed. The pipeline already has syft+grype+crane; this is mostly a new workflow plus a generated markdown/JSON artifact rendered on the portal. Replace the sed command with `go -C cli run ./cmd/clearcutt --catalog internal/testdata/catalog catalog summarize`.

verdict.note: Every factual claim checks out. docs/alternatives.md is 42 lines (finding said 43 — trivial off-by-one), names no concrete alternative (no Chainguard/apko/gcr.io/distroless/pkgs.dockerTools/multi-stage anywhere in the file), and its Category Comparison table is exactly the four generic rows quoted, with zero quantitative data. README.md:73 and docs/README.md:11 both make it the Engineering manager's "First document" with first command `sed -n '1,140p' docs/alternatives.md`, which indeed asks for 140 lines of a 42-line file. The repo does already generate the cited metrics per image: latestPackageCount and vulnSummary in site/src/data/catalog/index.json, and sbom.packageCount/sbom.packages in releases[].architectures[].sbom of site/src/data/catalog/images/*.json; syft/grype/crane appear in .github/workflows/publish-pages.yml and release.yml, so the recommendation is feasible with existing tooling. The one mitigating control: this is a documented deliberate decision, not an oversight — docs/analysis/decisions-needed.md:18 explicitly chose "category-level tradeoff comparison" over naming vendors (rationale in docs/analysis/clearcutt-audit.md:48: competitors' primitives are not unique, named CVE/size claims go stale) and recorded the residual risk. The finding acknowledges this, so it stands, but the documented decision plus the fact that this is a positioning/docs-quality issue (no functional or security impact) makes "high" severity inflated; medium is more defensible. The sed quirk is real but cosmetic. fable-review and main are identical for all cited files.

verifiedFindings.title: Evidence portal silently rewrites scanner identity in the served evidence JSON
verifiedFindings.detail: site/src/lib/catalog.ts defines publicArchPayload which rewrites `arch.vulnerabilities.scanner` from any 'grype*' value to the string 'vulnerability-check' and renames assertions ('Grype Vulnerability Gating' → 'Vulnerability check'). Because the static JSON route catalog/images/[id].json.ts serves loadImage() output, the rewrite lands in the published machine-readable evidence, not just UI labels — confirmed live: https://northcutted.github.io/clearcutt/catalog/images/java21-distroless.json returns scanner: "vulnerability-check" while sbom tool honestly reads "syft-1.44.0". This directly contradicts docs/trust/catalog-evidence.md ('Generated site labels should be read literally') and the core differentiator of 'inspectable evidence surfaces rather than opaque trust' (docs/alternatives.md:15-16). A skeptical auditor diffing the GitHub Release scan asset against the portal JSON sees a mutated scanner field and reasonably asks what else is rewritten. The replicated copy in the embedded template ships the same behavior to every fork.
verifiedFindings.recommendation: Delete the scanner/assertion renaming in publicArchPayload (and the vestigial 'credential broker'→'credential helper' replace — the source blurb in cli/internal/catalogbuild/model.go:79 already says 'credential helper'). Display scanner name, version, and dbBuiltAt verbatim; if a friendlier label is wanted, add a displayName alongside the untouched scanner field. Regenerate the embedded template (go generate ./...) so forks inherit the fix.

verdict.note: Every factual claim verified. site/src/lib/catalog.ts:37-58 (and the identical embedded template copy at cli/internal/sitetemplate/template/src/lib/catalog.ts) rewrites vulnerabilities.scanner from grype* to 'vulnerability-check' in publicArchPayload; the static route site/src/pages/catalog/images/[id].json.ts serves loadImage() output, so the rewrite lands in published machine-readable evidence. Confirmed end-to-end: on-disk source data has "scanner": "grype-0.112.0" while the live https://northcutted.github.io/clearcutt/catalog/images/java21-distroless.json returns "scanner": "vulnerability-check" with sbom tool honestly reading "syft-1.44.0". I searched for mitigating controls and found none: raw/scans/ in the catalog data is empty, no site route serves raw scan files, the verbatim-served evidence-manifest.json contains no scanner identity, and no doc discloses the mapping — the rewritten value is the only scanner identity the portal publishes. docs/trust/catalog-evidence.md:50 ("Generated site labels should be read literally") and docs/alternatives.md:15-16 (inspectable evidence vs opaque trust) say what the finding claims, and model.go:79 already says "credential helper", confirming the blurb replace is vestigial. One minor correction: the site-level assertion rename is mostly dead code because the Go generator (cli/internal/catalogbuild/record.go:84-92) already renames 'Grype Vulnerability Gating' to 'Vulnerability gate' before records reach the site (live JSON shows 'Vulnerability gate', not 'Vulnerability check') — which means scanner-identity scrubbing also happens upstream in the generator, slightly broadening rather than weakening the finding. High severity is justified in context: the product's stated differentiator is literal, inspectable evidence, and the recommendation (display verbatim, optional displayName, regenerate template) is sound.

unverifiedFindings.title: Architecture diagram 404s on the live About/Audit page (base-path bug, replicated into every fork)
unverifiedFindings.detail: about.astro:119 renders `` with a root-absolute path, but astro.config.mjs sets `base: '/clearcutt'`. Verified live: https://northcutted.github.io/supply-chain-flow.svg → 404 while https://northcutted.github.io/clearcutt/supply-chain-flow.svg → 200, so the supply-chain architecture diagram — on the exact page titled 'About & Audit Guide' that security reviewers are routed to — is a broken image. index.astro carefully computes a base-prefixed hrefFor() helper (index.astro:10,33-38), so this is an isolated miss. The bug is also baked into the embedded fork template (cli/internal/sitetemplate/template/src/pages/about.astro:119). Separately, docs/images/supply-chain-flow.svg is referenced by zero markdown files — the README and all of docs/ contain no architecture diagram at all (the only inline diagram is the 4-node mermaid sketch in docs/security-model.md:26-31).
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Prefix the asset with the base path (`${(import.meta.env.BASE_URL ?? '/').replace(/\/$/, '')}/supply-chain-flow.svg`) in both site/ and the embedded template, then regenerate. Embed docs/images/supply-chain-flow.svg in README.md (it is currently orphaned) and consider expanding the security-model mermaid into a full trust-boundary diagram for leadership audiences.

unverifiedFindings.title: ADR digest-pinning mandate is contradicted by every shipped template Dockerfile
unverifiedFindings.detail: docs/decisions.md ADR #2 states: 'All base image templates and production deployments must pin OCI image references using their immutable SHA-256 digest rather than standard mutable version tags.' But the committed templates use bare mutable tags — examples/clearcutt-template-java/Dockerfile:1 is `FROM ghcr.io/northcutted/clearcutt/clearcutt-java21:dev AS builder` and line 7 `FROM ...:distroless`; the generator hard-codes the same (app_template.go:176-177: `spec.DevImage = cfg.ImageName(spec.RuntimeLine) + ":dev"`), and getting-started.md's 'Manual Dockerfile Fallback' does too. The ADR's own rationale ('An attacker who gains write access to a registry can overwrite the tag') applies verbatim to these FROM lines. The certification policy's requireDigestPinned:true covers only the app image ref, not the base. A sharp reviewer will quote the ADR against the kit's own paved path.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Either (a) soften ADR #2 to describe digest pinning as the production posture and add an explicit 'pin your base' step to templates (the catalog already exposes latestManifestDigest; `clearcutt inspect` can print a copy-paste FROM line with @sha256), or (b) make `app template` resolve and emit digest-pinned FROM lines from the configured catalog with a comment noting the rebase workflow updates them. Option (a) is a one-day fix; (b) is the better showcase.

unverifiedFindings.title: Published catalog contract mislabels manifest-descriptor size as imageSize (15.6 kB for a 318 MiB image)
unverifiedFindings.detail: enrichmentArchitecture sets `size := descriptorSize` (the OCI manifest descriptor's byte size) and only falls back to the layer-sum when it is zero (catalog_enrich.go:397-399). Result in the live evidence JSON: java21-distroless reports imageSize: 15626 and release totalSize: 31253 while its layers sum to 333,577,839 bytes (318 MiB) — confirmed against https://northcutted.github.io/clearcutt/catalog/images/java21-distroless.json. The schema (image-record.v2.schema.json:61) gives no description, so any downstream consumer of this 'portable catalog artifact for policy, audit, and site rendering' (docs/platform-kit.md:136) will misread image size by four orders of magnitude. The unused LayersTable.astro:23 would render '98 layers · 15.6 kB' if ever wired up (the live page avoids it only because LayerExplorer.tsx recomputes from layer sums). Image size is also a headline differentiation metric that is currently absent from the portal because the recorded number is wrong.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Record both fields explicitly: keep manifestDescriptorSize if useful, and populate imageSize with the compressed layer sum (already computed as `total` in the same function). Add descriptions to the schema fields, bump the image-record schema patch version, and surface 'compressed size' on ImageHeader/catalog cards — small distroless sizes are a selling point worth rendering.

unverifiedFindings.title: 1,123 lines of internal 'not ready' audit history ship in docs/analysis/ — free ammunition for skeptics
unverifiedFindings.detail: docs/analysis/clearcutt-audit.md publicly states 'The project is not ready for broad, serious human feedback...' and lists 'What feels like marketing? "Every image signed, attested", ... "Vulnerability Free", "VERIFIED KEYLESS", and "non-falsifiable"', while post-hardening-readiness.md records a 'Brutal skeptic | NOT HAPPY' reviewer row and 'Screenshots remain deferred by owner direction.' The superseded-status banners are present and the transparency is admirable, but these files are one `ls docs/` away from the front door and are quotable out of context ('the project's own audit says the claims feel like marketing'). One leftover banned phrase also survives in product copy: 'Highly secure production hosting' at site/src/lib/image-metadata.ts:237, which the claims register (docs/audit-findings.md) explicitly disallows.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Reframe rather than delete: move the snapshots to docs/analysis/history/ with a short README that leads with the post-hardening verdict and frames the audit as the project's QA process (it genuinely is a strength), or distill them into one 'How we audit ourselves' doc and drop the raw reviewer-mood tables. Fix the 'Highly secure' string in image-metadata.ts to comply with the claims register.

unverifiedFindings.title: Zero visual or recorded demo artifacts — the showcase is 100% text
unverifiedFindings.detail: There is not a single screenshot, GIF, or asciinema recording anywhere in README.md or docs/ (grep for asciinema/.gif/.png across README and docs returns nothing). docs/demo.md:63-69 instead asks the reviewer to 'Capture screenshots of: docs front door role routing, CLI fixture-backed verify image, catalog homepage...' — i.e., the demo doc outsources the demo to the audience. The portal at northcutted.github.io/clearcutt is genuinely impressive (live evidence JSON, provenance blocks, vulnerability tables) but a leadership reviewer skimming the GitHub repo never sees it; the only visual asset, supply-chain-flow.svg, is orphaned in docs and broken on the live site (see separate finding). For 'wow-factor showcase quality' this is the largest cheap win available.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Record a 60-90s asciinema of the five clean-clone commands (list → inspect → verify image → app template → catalog site build) and convert to GIF for the README hero; add two screenshots (catalog matrix + java21-distroless evidence page) under docs/images/ and embed them in README.md and docs/demo.md. The fixture-backed commands are already deterministic, so the recording is reproducible in CI if desired.

unverifiedFindings.title: Dead components and terminology drift in the portal (replicated into the fork template)
unverifiedFindings.detail: TerminalSimulator.tsx (226 lines) and LayersTable.astro are imported by no page in site/src (grep confirms zero usages outside their own files), yet both are shipped twice — in site/ and inside the embedded template every fork scaffolds. Terminology also drifts: limitations.astro:110 headlines 'Credential Broker exposure' while its body and the rest of the site say 'credential helper' (the very term catalog.ts:23 rewrites), and the underlying core file is still core/lib/credential-broker.sh. Small, but this is the kind of inconsistency a reviewer notices on a project whose pitch is precision.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Delete TerminalSimulator.tsx and LayersTable.astro (or wire LayersTable in after fixing imageSize), pick one name for the credential component ('build-time credential helper' is already the public term) and align limitations.astro heading and core/lib/credential-broker.sh naming, then run go generate ./... so the embedded template tracks the cleanup.

strengths: The embedded site template cannot drift: cli/internal/sitetemplate/template/src is byte-identical to site/src (verified — diff shows only site/src/data differs) and is enforced by TestEmbeddedTemplateMatchesSite (cli/internal/sitetemplate/sitetemplate_test.go:32), the gold standard the schema copies should also adopt.

Schemas ship with every generated catalog: writeCatalogSchemaFiles (cli/internal/commands/catalog_schemas.go) emits all 7 versioned schemas into <catalog>/schemas/, and the 6 schemas shared between root schemas/ and the embedded set are currently byte-identical — consumers get a versioned contract alongside the data.

v1/v2 coexistence is managed migration, not cruft: versioned constants with doc comments (cli/internal/catalog/types.go:8-19), BuildIndex auto-selects v2 only when service/kind images exist (catalogbuild/index.go:66-82), validate accepts both and supports --schema-version pinning (catalog_validate.go:183-212), and pr-gate.yml:285-286 gates the mixed-kind fixture on the v2 versions in CI.

`clearcutt catalog validate` does real referential-integrity work beyond field checks: duplicate/orphan image-record detection, index-vs-latest-release evidence cross-checks per channel, and an evidence-manifest that must DeepEqual a rebuild from the image records (catalog_validate.go:137-181) — plus a global --strict flag that wires json.DisallowUnknownFields as a deliberate drift catcher (cli/internal/catalog/load.go:12-23).

Exceptions enforcement is in exact parity with its schema: the status enum (affected/not_affected/fixed/under_investigation/false_positive/accepted_risk) and the 7-value reason enum in cli/internal/commands/exceptions.go:202-211 match schemas/exceptions.schema.json:47-62 one-for-one, including apiVersion/kind gating.

The rebase attestation contract is duplicated correctly in both layers: schemas/rebase-attestation.schema.json's allOf if/then (allowed ⇒ developerSignatureVerified=true + non-empty developerIdentity) is mirrored exactly by Predicate.Validate() in cli/internal/attest/rebase.go:84-110 — dual-control encoded twice, consistently.

fleet.Config is a well-engineered single Go source of truth: defaults derivation from owner/repo, applyDefaults + Validate with actionable errors listing supported values, built-in runtime-line and service-template registries, and GitHub matrix generation all in one place (cli/internal/fleet/config.go).

Developer-experience touches like the catalog-not-found error (cli/internal/catalog/load.go:29-41) that tells users exactly how to generate, build, or point at the bundled fixture catalog — rare polish for a governance CLI.
wowIdeas: Make the shipped schemas executable: add github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 and have `catalog validate` (and a pr-gate + publish-pages step) validate index.json, images/*.json, and evidence-manifest.json against the embedded schemas. One dependency converts the schemas/ directory from documentation into enforced contract — and would have caught every drift finding in this review automatically.

Single-source the contract: generate the site's zod definitions from the JSON Schemas (json-schema-to-zod) and add a golden Go test that round-trips each fixture catalog through the catalog package's marshal/unmarshal and re-validates against the schema, killing the three-way Go/zod/schema divergence permanently.

Self-attesting catalogs: stamp generator.commit/version from runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo() (vcs.revision works on any git build, no ldflags needed), then have publish-pages sign the catalog index with the same cosign keyless flow used for images — the evidence portal's data becomes evidence itself, displayed as a 'catalog provenance' badge on the site's About page.

Publish the schemas at their $id URLs (https://clearcutt.dev/schemas/...) via the existing Pages site and add a yaml-language-server modeline to clearcutt.yaml — forks get live editor validation of fleet configs and external policy tooling can $ref the catalog contract directly.

Add `clearcutt catalog migrate --to v2` that promotes v1 runtime records to v2 (kind: runtime, explicit nulls), plus a schemaVersion badge per image on the site — making the v1→v2 transition a visible, finishable migration instead of a permanent mixed state.

verifiedFindings.title: Published catalog index violates its own shipped v2 schema: required `kind` missing on 36 of 39 image summaries
verifiedFindings.detail: catalog-index.v2.schema.json lists "kind" in CatalogImageSummary.required (lines 189-204). But the generator's ImageSummary marshals it as `Kind string `json:"kind,omitempty"`` (catalogbuild/model.go:215) and runtime images never get Kind set — only service images do. BuildIndex flips the whole index to v2 whenever ANY image is v2 (`if img.Kind != "" || img.Service != nil { hasV2Image = true }`, index.go:68; `schemaVersion = catalog.CatalogIndexSchemaVersionV2`, index.go:81). The real generated catalog confirms it: site/src/data/catalog/index.json declares `"schemaVersion": "clearcutt.catalog.index/v2"` yet 36 of 39 image summaries (every runtime image: coreLTS-dev, java21-dev, node22-*, ...) have no `kind` key; only postgres16/valkey8/oauth2-proxy7 do. Nothing catches this: the CLI's own validator defaults empty kind to "runtime" (`normalizedKind` in catalog/validate.go:48-54) and the site's zod does `.optional().default('runtime')` (site/src/lib/catalog-schema.ts:339). Any consumer who runs the schemas the catalog itself ships under schemas/ will see the flagship artifact fail validation.
verifiedFindings.recommendation: In SummarizeImageForIndex (cli/internal/catalogbuild/record.go:202) and the v2 record path, explicitly set Kind to "runtime" when the index is emitted as v2 (or drop omitempty and normalize at build time). Add a regression test that marshals a mixed-catalog index and asserts every images[] entry has a kind when schemaVersion is v2.

verdict.note: Every claim checked out. (1) /Users/eddie/Development/clearcutt-images/schemas/catalog-index.v2.schema.json lists "kind" in CatalogImageSummary.required (line 191) and images[] items $ref that definition (line 77); identical copies ship at cli/internal/catalog/schemas/ and site/src/data/catalog/schemas/. (2) cli/internal/catalogbuild/model.go:215 has `Kind string `json:"kind,omitempty"``. (3) cli/internal/catalogbuild/index.go:68 flips hasV2Image when any image has Kind or Service, and line 81 sets the whole index to v2. (4) Runtime records never set Kind: runtimeRecordTarget (record.go:66-82) omits it while only BuildServiceImageRecord sets Kind "service" (record.go:389), and SummarizeImageForIndex copies img.Kind verbatim (record.go:272). (5) I parsed site/src/data/catalog/index.json: schemaVersion is "clearcutt.catalog.index/v2", 39 images, exactly 36 lack a "kind" key, only postgres16/valkey8/oauth2-proxy7 carry kind:"service" — matching the finding's numbers. (6) No mitigating control exists: go.mod pulls in no JSON Schema validator; the CI gate (.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml:285) runs `catalog validate`, whose normalizedKind (cli/internal/catalog/validate.go:48-54) silently defaults empty kind to "runtime"; site/src/lib/catalog-schema.ts:339 likewise does `.optional().default('runtime')`; cli/internal/catalog/schema_files_test.go only asserts the schema files are bundled, never that generated output conforms. So the published artifact genuinely fails the schema it ships. Only quibble: severity "high" is arguable — both in-repo consumers tolerate the omission, so impact is limited to external consumers validating against the shipped schema; medium-high would also be defensible, but for a project whose product is verifiable supply-chain evidence, the self-contradiction is material.

verifiedFindings.title: All four JSON Schemas families are decorative — no JSON Schema validator runs anywhere in CLI, site, or CI
verifiedFindings.detail: The repo maintains three hand-written parallel contracts: JSON Schemas (schemas/ + embedded cli/internal/catalog/schemas/), Go structs (cli/internal/catalog/types.go), and zod (site/src/lib/catalog-schema.ts) — but no code path ever executes the JSON Schemas. cli/go.mod has no jsonschema dependency (only cobra, go-containerregistry, sigs.k8s.io/yaml). `clearcutt catalog validate` is entirely hand-rolled structural checking (catalog_validate.go), the site parses with its own zod definitions (catalog.ts:94,105), and CI only runs `catalog validate --schema-version ...` (pr-gate.yml:285-286), which merely string-compares the schemaVersion field. Meanwhile writeCatalogSchemaFiles (catalog_schemas.go) ships the schemas into every generated catalog as the public contract, and docs/catalog-schema.md presents them as the spec. The result is exactly the drift documented in the other findings: the published artifact fails its own published schema and nobody notices. clearcutt-fleet.schema.json, certification-policy.schema.json, and exceptions.schema.json are likewise enforced only by parallel Go logic.
verifiedFindings.recommendation: Add a JSON Schema engine (e.g. github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6) and make `catalog validate` run the embedded schemas against index.json, every images/*.json, and evidence-manifest.json in addition to the structural checks. Add a Go test that validates all three testdata catalogs and a freshly generated catalog against the schemas, and a publish-pages.yml step that schema-validates the catalog artifact before deploy.

verdict.note: Every cited fact checks out. cli/go.mod depends only on cobra, go-containerregistry, and sigs.k8s.io/yaml — no jsonschema library, and no .go file in the repo imports one (the lone santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema entry in go.work.sum is a /go.mod-only graph hash, not built code). cli/internal/commands/catalog_validate.go is entirely hand-rolled structural checking, and its --schema-version handling (validateIndexSchemaVersion/validateImageSchemaVersion) is plain string comparison against constants. site/src/lib/catalog-schema.ts is 389 lines of zod; site/src/lib/catalog.ts parses with CatalogIndex.parse (~line 94) and ImageRecord.parse (~line 105); site/package.json has zod but no validator (ajv appears only as a transitive astro dep in the lockfile). pr-gate.yml lines 285-286 run exactly the two `catalog validate --schema-version ...` commands claimed, and no workflow (pr-gate, publish-pages, scheduled-scan), script, Makefile target, or core/ pipeline step runs a JSON Schema engine. writeCatalogSchemaFiles (catalog_schemas.go:10-25) ships the embedded schemas into every generated catalog and docs/catalog-schema.md presents them as the published contract; the only related test (schema_files_test.go) merely checks the embedded files exist and are non-empty. Fleet/certification/exceptions schemas are likewise backed only by parallel Go logic (cli/internal/fleet/config.go, commands/certify.go, commands/exceptions.go). I found no mitigating control, and I empirically confirmed the claimed consequence: running ajv against the published artifact, site/src/data/catalog/index.json (schemaVersion clearcutt.catalog.index/v2) fails its own shipped catalog-index.v2.schema.json because every images[] entry lacks the schema-required "kind" property (schemas/catalog-index.v2.schema.json:191). Only quibble: the phrase that CI "merely string-compares the schemaVersion field" undersells that `catalog validate` also runs the full hand-rolled structural checks — but the finding acknowledges those elsewhere, so this is phrasing, not a factual error. High severity is justified: the schemas are the shipped public contract and the published artifact demonstrably violates them with nothing in CLI, site, or CI able to notice.

verifiedFindings.title: Published evidence catalog stamps generator as version "dev", commit "unknown"
verifiedFindings.detail: stampCatalogIndexMetadata writes `index.Generator = &catalog.CatalogGenerator{Name: "clearcutt", Version: catalogbuild.FirstNonEmptyStr(Version, "dev"), Commit: "unknown"}` — Commit is hardcoded to "unknown" with no code path that ever fills it. Version is only injected by release.yml:394 (`-ldflags="... -X github.com/northcutted/clearcutt/internal/commands.Version=$VERSION"`), but the Pages pipeline that actually publishes the catalog builds with a bare `go build -o ../clearcutt ./cmd/clearcutt` (publish-pages.yml:54 and :190). Ground truth from the generated data: site/src/data/catalog/index.json contains `"generator": {"name": "clearcutt", "version": "dev", "commit": "unknown"}`. For a platform whose whole pitch is evidence and provenance, the evidence index's own generator provenance is unversioned and untraceable — and this is the version-drift ground truth across workspaces: the released CLI knows its version, the catalog/site pipeline does not.
verifiedFindings.recommendation: Derive version/commit via runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo() (vcs.revision, vcs.time, module version) as a fallback in stampCatalogIndexMetadata so even plain `go build` binaries stamp the real commit; additionally pass the same -ldflags in publish-pages.yml. Surface generator version/commit on the site About page as a trust signal.

verdict.note: Every factual claim checks out. cli/internal/commands/catalog_cmd.go:246-263 contains stampCatalogIndexMetadata with Commit hardcoded to "unknown" (line 254) and Version falling back to "dev"; no code anywhere in cli/ uses runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo or vcs.revision, so nothing ever fills Commit. root.go:8-9 declares Version="dev"; release.yml:394 is the only ldflags injection (Version only); publish-pages.yml builds the CLI with bare `go build` at lines 54 and 190 and then runs `./clearcutt catalog build` (lines 132/139), so the Pages-published catalog is stamped dev/unknown — confirmed by the generated site/src/data/catalog/index.json on disk (gitignored artifact, generated 2026-06-08) containing exactly {"name":"clearcutt","version":"dev","commit":"unknown"}. I searched for mitigating controls and found none: no script or workflow post-processes the generator field. Two caveats on severity: (1) the homepage's "Generator" row (site/src/pages/index.astro:116) hardcodes "ClearCutt static portal" and never renders the dev/unknown values, and (2) image-level trust (cosign signatures, SLSA provenance, SBOMs) is verified independently of this metadata, so nothing security-critical depends on the generator stamp. The finding is real and well-evidenced, but "high" overstates it — this is a provenance-completeness/credibility gap in informational metadata, best rated medium.

unverifiedFindings.title: v1 catalog emission self-invalidates: index stamping round-trip silently drops schema-required Lifecycle/RuntimeContract keys
unverifiedFindings.detail: catalog-index.v1.schema.json requires Lifecycle to contain `deprecatedAt`, `eolAt`, `reason` (required list, lines 135-142) and RuntimeContract to contain all 8 keys including `defaultEntrypoint` (lines 160-169). The writer types in catalogbuild always emit them (lifecycle.go:10-29, no omitempty), but stampCatalogIndexMetadata — called after every `catalog generate`/`catalog build` (catalog_cmd.go:175,734,744,806; catalog_build.go:109) — re-loads index.json through the reader types and rewrites it. Those use `*string` with omitempty (types.go:150-152 `json:"deprecatedAt,omitempty"` etc.), so null values are dropped. Empirically verified: round-tripping the fixture index through these types yields `{"status":"active","support":"lts","productionAllowed":true}` — three required keys gone. rust/cc images also lose `defaultEntrypoint` (determineRuntimeContract returns nil for them; confirmed in real data: rust1.95-dev runtimeContract has 7 keys, no defaultEntrypoint). The current production catalog escapes only because services flip it to v2, whose relaxed required lists tolerate the omissions — a fork building a runtime-only fleet emits a v1 index that fails the v1 schema it ships.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Either drop omitempty from Lifecycle/RuntimeContract pointer fields in cli/internal/catalog/types.go (emit explicit nulls, matching the catalogbuild writer and the v1 schema), or relax the v1 schema's required lists to match v2. Then add the schema-validation test from the main finding to lock it.

unverifiedFindings.title: clearcutt-fleet.schema.json is referenced nowhere and rejects the documented `runtimeLines` feature via additionalProperties:false
unverifiedFindings.detail: schemas/clearcutt-fleet.schema.json sets top-level `"additionalProperties": false` (line 6) but defines no `runtimeLines` property. The Go Config explicitly supports it (`RuntimeLines []RuntimeLine `json:"runtimeLines,omitempty"``, fleet/config.go:40, with full validation in runtimeLineMap), and docs/extending-clearcutt.md:52 documents that `clearcutt runtime scaffold` "writes a custom `runtimeLines` entry" into clearcutt.yaml. So any fork that uses the advertised extension mechanism produces a fleet config that fails the published schema. The schema is also wholly unenforced: grepping the repo, the only reference to clearcutt-fleet.schema.json is its own $id — no Go code, workflow, Makefile target, or editor wiring (e.g. yaml-language-server modeline in clearcutt.yaml) ever loads it. The schema's enums also drift from Go: `matrix.languages` is free-form in the schema but Go restricts to supportedRuntimeLines+custom; `templates.runtimes` is schema-enum'd to [java,node,python,go] while Go never validates it at all (Config.Validate has no templates check, config.go:508-579).
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Add a `runtimeLines` property (mirroring RuntimeLine: id/language/version/appTemplateRuntime/description/packageCandidates/devPackages/omitInProduction/smoke) to the schema, add a `# yaml-language-server: $schema=...` modeline to clearcutt.yaml for editor validation, and validate the schema against clearcutt.yaml in a Go test or pr-gate step so it cannot drift again.

unverifiedFindings.title: Fixture catalogs are stale against the published schemas and don't match current generator output
unverifiedFindings.detail: The primary fixture (cli/internal/testdata/catalog) fails the published v1 schemas on multiple required fields: index.json has no `schemaVersion`, `generator`, `source`, or `summary` (all four are in catalog-index.v1.schema.json's required list, lines 5-20, and the current generator always stamps them via stampCatalogIndexMetadata); images/java21-distroless.json has no `schemaVersion` (required const in image-record.v1.schema.json:5-18); and its SBOM packages lack the required `cpes` array (e.g. `{"name": "openssl", "version": "3.0.8", "license": "Apache-2.0", "supplier": "Nix", "spdxId": "SPDXRef-openssl"}` — `cpes` is required by both package-entry.v1.schema.json:7 and image-record.v1.schema.json:54, and the real writer spdxPackageOut always emits it). dev-catalog has the same gaps. Yet `./clearcutt --catalog cli/internal/testdata/catalog catalog validate` passes with 0 errors — demonstrating the Go validator cannot detect published-schema violations. Also, the mixed-catalog fixture marks its runtime record as `clearcutt.catalog.image/v2`, while the production generator emits runtime records as v1 under a v2 index (record.go:75 vs site/src/data/catalog/images/coreLTS-dev.json = v1), so the CI fixture doesn't exercise the shape production actually produces.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Regenerate the fixtures from the current generator (or hand-patch schemaVersion/generator/source/summary/cpes), add a runtime-record-at-v1-under-v2-index case to mixed-catalog, and add the schema-validation test so fixtures can never silently drift from the published contract again.

unverifiedFindings.title: CLI run from cli/ scatters generated trees (cli/core, cli/site, cli/docs, cli/examples) — papered over by .gitignore instead of fixed
unverifiedFindings.detail: .gitignore:36-42 says it outright: "# Accidental nested output roots created when commands run from cli/. The canonical project roots are /site, /examples, /docs, and /core." followed by ignores for /cli/site/, /cli/examples/, /cli/docs/, /cli/core/. These directories really exist on disk: cli/core/lib/platform-metadata.nix contains leftover test branding (`repoPath = "acme/platform"`, `productName = "Platform"`) from a `platform init` run, and cli/site/src/data holds full SBOM dumps for v0.7.0 and v0.9.8 plus catalog records — megabytes of stale generated data shadowing the real site/src/data. Root cause: commands resolve output paths relative to cwd (e.g. platform.go:102 `filepath.Join(root, "core", "lib", "platform-metadata.nix")`), so running from cli/ writes a parallel universe. cli/core is NOT a duplicate of core/ in any designed sense — it is debris — but anyone auditing the repo (or an agent grepping it) will read the acme/platform metadata and stale SBOMs as real, and a fork could ship them.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Make the CLI resolve the repo root (walk up for go.work / clearcutt.yaml) instead of trusting cwd, or refuse to run mutating commands when cwd basename is cli/ inside a repo. Delete the existing cli/core, cli/site, cli/docs, cli/examples trees and ensure tests use t.TempDir().

unverifiedFindings.title: Root schemas/ directory drifts from the embedded/emitted schema set: missing evidence-manifest.v1, plus two orphaned legacy duplicates
unverifiedFindings.detail: The CLI embeds and emits 7 schemas (cli/internal/catalog/schemas/, guarded by TestSchemaArtifactsIncludesVersionedSchemas), including evidence-manifest.v1.schema.json — which does not exist in the root schemas/ directory at all, even though docs/catalog-schema.md:48 documents it as part of the generated layout. Conversely, root schemas/ contains two files the CLI does not embed and nothing references: catalog.schema.json (byte-identical to catalog-index.v1.schema.json) and image-record.schema.json (identical to image-record.v1.schema.json except its $refs point at `catalog.schema.json#/definitions/...` instead of `catalog-index.v1.schema.json#/...`). The 6 shared files are currently byte-identical between root and embedded copies, but no test or CI check guards that — unlike the site template, which has TestEmbeddedTemplateMatchesSite.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Delete schemas/catalog.schema.json and schemas/image-record.schema.json, copy evidence-manifest.v1.schema.json into root schemas/, and add a small Go test asserting root schemas/ and the embedded set are identical (mirroring the site-template drift test).

unverifiedFindings.title: Index `tiers` taxonomy omits the "service" tier used by its own images
unverifiedFindings.detail: tierList() builds the index's `tiers` array from the fixed gatherTierOrder = ["dev", "slim", "distroless"] (model.go:76, 115-122). The v2 schema's TierInfo enum includes "service" (catalog-index.v2.schema.json:95) and the real published index contains three images with `"tier": "service"` (postgres16, valkey8, oauth2-proxy7) — but its `tiers` array lists only dev/slim/distroless. Any consumer that renders tier filters or legends from index.tiers (the documented purpose: "tier summaries") will miss the service tier that a third of the v2 feature set lives in.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Append a `{id: "service", name: "Service", blurb: ...}` entry to tierList() when the catalog contains service images (i.e., when the index is v2 with kind=service entries).

unverifiedFindings.title: Site zod contract drifts from v2 schema and Go types: strips latestManifestDigest, over-strict lifecycle.support enum
unverifiedFindings.detail: Two concrete mismatches between site/src/lib/catalog-schema.ts and the rest of the stack: (1) the zod CatalogIndex images object (lines 336-387) has no `latestManifestDigest` field, while the Go generator always emits it (catalogbuild/model.go:221 `json:"latestManifestDigest"`, no omitempty), the v2 schema documents it (catalog-index.v2.schema.json:213), and the real data carries it (site/src/data/catalog/index.json:133 etc.). zod's default parse strips unknown keys, so the digest is silently discarded from the parsed index — the denormalization built for cheap digest display can never reach a site component. (2) zod Lifecycle.support is the strict v1 enum `['lts','current','preview','legacy','unsupported']` (line 142), but catalog-index.v2.schema.json deliberately relaxed support to a free string (line 135) and Go never validates it; a fork with a custom support label (e.g. fleet services' free-text ServiceLifecycle.Support) passes the CLI and the v2 schema but throws at site build time in CatalogIndex.parse (catalog.ts:94). Note the identical copies in cli/internal/sitetemplate/template/src/lib/catalog-schema.ts inherit both issues.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Add `latestManifestDigest: NullableString` to the zod images object, and relax `support` to z.string() (or enum-with-fallback) to match the v2 contract. The sitetemplate drift test will force the embedded copy to follow.

unverifiedFindings.title: Docs pin CLI/image versions 7+ releases behind the current tag
unverifiedFindings.detail: Latest git tag is v0.17.0, but docs/certification.md pins `VERSION="v0.10.2"` (line 77) and `CLEARCUTT_VERSION: "v0.10.2"` (line 162) in the two copy-paste supply-chain install snippets, and docs/app-lifecycle.md uses `:v0.2.2-distroless` image tags in 9 examples (lines 134-328). The comments rightly say to pin and bump deliberately, but for showcase docs a 7-minor-version-stale pin reads as unmaintained, and users copying the snippet get an old CLI. scripts/validate-doc-commands.sh already greps docs for drift but does not check version currency.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Add a check to scripts/validate-doc-commands.sh (or the release workflow) that flags doc version pins older than N releases, and bump the pins as part of the release checklist (release.yml could sed them automatically).

unverifiedFindings.title: Workflows hardcode Go 1.26 in two places instead of go-version-file
unverifiedFindings.detail: pr-gate.yml and e2e-runtimes.yml correctly use `go-version-file: 'cli/go.mod'`, but cve-patch-agent.yml:65 and publish-pages.yml:47,183 hardcode `go-version: '1.26'`. Consistent today (go.work and cli/go.mod both say go 1.26), but it is the classic cross-workspace version-drift vector: the next toolchain bump in go.mod will leave the CVE agent and the Pages publisher building with a different Go than CI gates.
unverifiedFindings.recommendation: Switch the three hardcoded steps to `go-version-file: 'cli/go.mod'` with `cache-dependency-path: 'cli/go.sum'`, matching pr-gate.yml.

gaps: [high] No reviewer audited the GitHub repo-level controls the whole trust story bottoms out on: `main` has NO branch protection (`gh api repos/northcutted/clearcutt/branches/main/protection` returns 404 'Branch not protected') and NO rulesets (`/rulesets` returns `[]`), yet /Users/eddie/Development/clearcutt-images/.github/workflows/release.yml triggers on `push: branches: [main]` (lines 5-8) and pins the release identity to `refs/heads/main` (lines 35-39). The only human control is the `release-gate` job's `environment: production # <-- Manual approval gate here!` (line 73), whose protection rule (per `gh api .../environments`) has a single required reviewer (the maintainer) with `prevent_self_review: false`. Net effect: an unreviewed direct push to main can be self-approved into a fully signed, SLSA-attested release, and the 20KB pr-gate.yml suite is purely advisory because no status checks are required anywhere. The docs never close this hole either: docs/fork-validation.md lines 49-50 tell forks to create the `production` environment with required reviewers, but 'branch protection', 'protected branch', and 'ruleset' have zero grep hits across docs/, FORKING.md, and README.md — forks inherit the same gap by following the checklist.

[high] No SECURITY.md or vulnerability disclosure policy exists anywhere in the repo (verified with `find` across the tree excluding node_modules/.git: zero hits for SECURITY*, and zero hits for CODE_OF_CONDUCT*, CODEOWNERS*, PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE*, ISSUE_TEMPLATE, CHANGELOG*, NOTICE*). docs/security-model.md covers trust boundaries and non-claims (sections '1. Core Security Assurances' through '3. Security Model Limitations & Non-Claims') but contains no reporting channel — greps for 'security@', 'disclosure', and 'report vulnerability' across security-model.md, README.md, and CONTRIBUTING.md return nothing. A repo whose pitch is hardened, evidence-backed images gives security researchers no way to report a vulnerability privately, and GitHub's Security tab will show 'no policy'.

[medium] No dependency-update automation for the platform's own toolchain: there is no .github/dependabot.yml or renovate config, and the GitHub API confirms `dependabot_security_updates: disabled`. This compounds with scripts/validate-workflow-hardening.sh, which ENFORCES immutable SHA pins on every action ref ('workflow and composite action references must be pinned to immutable SHAs') — pins that nothing will ever bump. site/package-lock.json (291KB: astro, react 19, zod...), cli/go.sum, and core/flake.lock all have no automated update path (no `nix flake update` workflow exists; flake.lock appears in workflows only inside cache keys). The project that runs scheduled CVE scans and an automated patch agent for the images it ships has zero patch automation for the toolchain that builds and signs them.

[medium] Community/governance scaffolding is entirely absent for an open-source showcase: /Users/eddie/Development/clearcutt-images/.github contains only actions/, codex/, workflows/, and copilot-instructions.md — no CODEOWNERS, no issue templates, no PR template, no CODE_OF_CONDUCT, no CHANGELOG, despite `has_issues: true` and a README addressed to 'Open-source evaluator'. The gap is sharpened by .agents/reviewers/ shipping 18 reviewer persona TOMLs (security-auditor.toml, release-engineer.toml, etc.) — the repo defines richer review routing for AI agents than for human contributors.

[medium] The AI-agent operations layer (.agents/, .codex/, .github/codex/prompts/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) was examined by no dimension, and its generated artifacts are ungated: .agents/sync.sh compiles .agents/context/*.md into .github/copilot-instructions.md and .vscode/tasks.json, but no workflow runs `make agent-sync` or sync.sh (zero grep hits in .github/workflows and scripts/), so the 14KB copilot-instructions.md can drift silently (it is currently in sync — verified by diff). Worse, `git ls-files .vscode` is empty — the generated tasks.json is untracked, so fresh clones lack the documented VS Code tasks — and its default test task points at `./.claude/skills/test-clearcutt/scripts/verify.sh`, which is excluded by the `.claude/*` line in .gitignore and therefore does not exist in any clone. sync.sh also does `mkdir -p .claude/skills` (line ~29) and never writes anything into it.

[medium] Drift enforcement is sampled, not comprehensive: scripts/validate-doc-commands.sh hardcodes an 11-file docs allowlist (docs=(README.md docs/README.md ... docs/trust/catalog-evidence.md)) plus 2 site pages, leaving the Makefile, FORKING.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, .agents/runbooks/*.md, and every examples/*/README.md outside any command-drift gate. Similarly, site/src and cli/internal/sitetemplate/template/src are full duplicates (verified `diff -rq`: identical except site/src/data) with no equivalence check in pr-gate.yml — only a shared paths-filter trigger (line 68). This single pattern is the root cause behind the stale-pin and fixture-drift findings other dimensions reported independently.

[low] LICENSE is Apache-2.0 but no source file in cli/cmd, cli/internal, or core carries an SPDX identifier or Apache license header (grep for 'SPDX-License' and 'Licensed under the Apache' returns nothing), and there is no NOTICE file — weak provenance hygiene for a supply-chain-provenance product.

[verification] README 'First Proof From A Clean Clone' claims hold: all three commands were executed and pass — `go -C cli run ./cmd/clearcutt --catalog internal/testdata/catalog list` (returns the 1-row fixture catalog), the full `verify image java21-distroless --require-signature --require-sbom --require-provenance --max-critical 0 --max-high 3 --allow-preview` (10/10 checks PASS, exit 0), and `platform status --output "$PWD" --fleet-config clearcutt.yaml` (29 checks, all pass). One cosmetic inconsistency observed: for the same fixture record, `list` reports ARCHES 'amd64,arm64' while `verify image` prints 'architectures present: amd64'.
crossCuttingObservations: The repo enforces its trust chain exhaustively at the file level (29-check `platform status`, validate-workflow-hardening.sh, validate-doc-commands.sh, pr-gate matrix) but the GitHub host-platform layer everything bottoms out on is unconfigured: no branch protection, no required status checks, no rulesets, dependabot disabled. Every per-dimension reviewer audited file contents; none could see that the gates are optional because nothing requires them to pass before code reaches the release branch.

Remediation is asymmetric by design blind spot: scheduled-scan.yml + cve-patch-agent.yml + core/overlays patch CVEs in the SHIPPED images, while the toolchain that builds and signs them (npm deps in site/, Go modules in cli/, nixpkgs in core/flake.lock, SHA-frozen GitHub Actions) has zero update automation. An auditor pitching this as a supply-chain showcase will notice the build toolchain is the least-patched component in the system.

Drift gates are hand-picked samples rather than invariants — an 11-doc allowlist in validate-doc-commands.sh, fixed-string checks in validate-workflow-hardening.sh, no site/-to-sitetemplate equivalence check — which predicts and explains the independent stale-version, stale-fixture, and schema-drift findings reported by the cli-dx, showcase-docs, and schemas-consistency dimensions. The fix is one pattern (generate-and-diff gates over whole surfaces), not a dozen point fixes.

There is a substantial, polished AI-agent operations layer (.agents/ with 18 reviewer personas, 6 skills, 4 runbooks, a sync compiler; .codex/config.toml with multi-agent settings; .github/codex/prompts/) that no review dimension covered. It is simultaneously an unadvertised showcase differentiator and the least-gated surface in the repo: its generated outputs are untracked or unverified in CI, and it references gitignored paths — mirroring, for human contributors, the exact doc-drift failure mode the project gates everywhere else.

The .gitignore accretes exceptions for tool misbehavior rather than the tools being fixed: a 15MB `clearcutt` binary and `result` Nix symlink at the repo root, a second 13MB binary plus ~7MB of coverage artifacts inside cli/, and the /cli/site,/cli/core,/cli/docs,/cli/examples stray-tree entries — generalizing the cli-dx finding that '.gitignore codifies the bug' from one case to a repo-wide habit.

Positive signals no dimension recorded: secret scanning and push protection are enabled on the repo, the `production` environment approval gate genuinely exists and fronts all publish jobs, all README first-proof commands work from a clean checkout, and the copilot-instructions/agents-context pair is currently in sync — the showcase's biggest residual risks are configuration and governance gaps, not broken commands.
